findings.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — Unconditionally indexing the category query’s first row aborts migration when embed_category is unset or references a deleted category, before the uncategorized fallback can run.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Legacy hosts are inserted without normalization, so previously supported values such as https://example.com fail hostname-only lookups and break existing embeds after upgrade.
app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Validation limits top-level domains to five letters, rejecting previously supported valid hosts such as example.museum and example.technology.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Validation accepts hosts containing ports, but lookup compares them against URI#host, which excludes ports, so entries such as example.com:8080 never match requests.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — Validation limits top-level domains to five letters, rejecting previously supported valid hosts such as example.museum and example.technology.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/embeddable_host.rb line 2 a regex validation: `validates_format_of :host, :with => /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`. The `[a-z]{2,5}` part limits TLDs to 2-5 characters. Valid TLDs like .museum (6 chars), .technology (10 chars), and many new gTLDs would be rejected. This is a real bug that restricts valid hosts from being added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — Validation accepts hosts containing ports, but lookup compares them against URI#host, which excludes ports, so entries such as example.com:8080 never match requests.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real inconsistency in the code. Looking at the diff, the validation regex in embeddable_host.rb (line 2) accepts hosts with ports: `/\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\/i`. However, the `record_for_host` method (lines 10-17) uses `uri.host` which returns only the hostname without the port. The `before_validation` callback strips the protocol and path but does NOT strip the port from the stored host value. So if a user enters 'example.com:8080', it gets stored as 'example.com:8080', but when checking `host_allowed?`, the code compares against `uri.host` which would be just 'example.com', causing the lookup to fail. This is a legitimate bug where hosts with ports would never match.
